title: MIST labeled fault-case (C2 benchmark)
description: One labeled case in the MIST open-source benchmark of masked-downstream / data-integrity faults. A case records the target (write endpoint, dependency, read-back GET), how the fault was produced, the ground-truth label, and each oracle's EXPECTED VERDICT. Verdict semantics: 'flag' = the oracle reports a fault on this case; 'no_flag' = the oracle reports clean; 'not_applicable' = the oracle does not run on this case. An oracle is CORRECT on a case iff (verdict == flag) == (ground_truth.label == positive). Precision/recall/FP for any oracle are therefore computable directly from the corpus.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS schema the case was authored against (semver).

stratum.description: 1 = positive ground truth (injected/replicated/vendor, known label). 2 = benign trap (designed degradation / eventual consistency, label=negative). 3 = adjudicated wild traffic (label set by human raters).

fault_class.description: Surface phenomenon under test (NOT the genuine/benign verdict). 'none' = clean control run.

capture_status.description: 'specified' = designed, label known by construction, traces/read-back NOT yet recorded. 'captured' = control/fault traces + read-back recorded on a live deploy (provenance paths populated).

deploy.description: How it is deployed (e.g. k8s/minikube make deploy).

entry_endpoint.description: The externally-reachable endpoint MIST drives. A write (POST/PUT) for data-integrity cases; may be a read (GET) for swallowed-downstream cases.

kind.description: What the write depends on and where the fault sits.

readback_endpoint.description: The black-box GET used to verify the write landed. Required for data-integrity classes.

mechanism.description: How the surface phenomenon is produced. 'none' = clean control. 'natural' = designed-degradation path that exists in the unmodified SUT (no injection).

config.description: Reproducible knobs (env flags, toxiproxy rule, vendor feature flag). Free-form.

injected_by.description: Provenance, e.g. branch@commit that adds the injector.

trigger_input.description: The input that drives the case (e.g. 'valid route, >=2 existing stations').

label.description: positive = genuine data-integrity / masked defect. negative = benign (clean, designed degradation, or eventually-consistent-then-correct).

rationale.description: Why this label holds. For negatives, state the benign mechanism (e.g. designed fallback, optional dependency, eventual consistency) per the rubric.

source.description: How the label is grounded: by_construction (we injected it), replicated (TrainTicket F-corpus), vendor (OTel-Demo fault flag), adjudicated (human-rated, stratum 3), natural (documented designed-degradation path).

control_trace.description: Path to the control-run trace (fault OFF). null until captured.

fault_trace.description: Path to the fault-run trace (fault ON). null until captured.

readback_response.description: Path to the recorded read-back GET response. null until captured.

adjudication.description: Stratum-3 only: human-rater metadata. null for strata 1-2.

adjudicator.description: Third rater who resolved disagreement, if any.

verdict.description: Expected oracle output on this case. flag = reports a fault; no_flag = reports clean; not_applicable = oracle does not run here.
